correctness.rationale: On the \(a=1\) chart a polynomial change \(w=f-be-cd\) identifies \(F=w^2-4bcde\). Euler and the chain rule show the projective Jacobian ideal equals \(w,bcd,bce,bde,cde\); this is the intersection of six coordinate-pair prime ideals by the monomial support criterion. Permutation symmetry carries these exact identities to all six projective coordinate charts. The six vertex germs have tetrahedral Stanley-Reisner Hilbert series \((1+2t+3t^2)/(1-t)^2\) and multiplicity 6; connectedness of the tetrahedral graph establishes Cohen-Macaulayness. Exact symbolic computation reconstructed determinant/derivatives and checked finite degrees; the general proof does not infer infinity from sampling.
